_what: One row per inbound channel. This is the connection register: what the mechanism is, what we control, what the provider controls, what is still missing, and who has to do something about it. Nothing here activates anything. A channel becomes live by configuring credentials and a webhook at the provider, verifying, and switching mode from test to live - not by changing code.

_readiness.not_prepared: No adapter exists on our side.
_readiness.ready_for_configuration: Our side is finished. It needs credentials and a provider setting, nothing more.
_readiness.waiting_for_external_access: Our side is finished but somebody outside this repository must grant access, approve an app, or answer a question first.
_readiness.manual_only: The provider offers no inbound mechanism we can rely on. A person enters it by hand, and that is the design, not a gap.
_readiness.capability_unconfirmed: We do not know whether the provider can do this. EXTERNAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED before anything is promised.

_modes: Every channel has a mode: off, test or live. Only 'test' accepts a simulated payload. 'live' additionally requires real credentials to be present, and nothing in this repository can set it.
_idempotency: Every adapter declares an externalId. The inbound table has a unique index on (channel, external_id), so the same provider event delivered twice is stored once. Providers retry; that is normal and must never make two people.

website.label: Website form
website.mechanism: We publish an endpoint. The website posts to it.
website.rateLimit: Ours to set. A public form needs a spam control in front of it.
providerControls: nothing - this is our own website
website.externalActionRequired: Whoever maintains the website points the form at the endpoint and sets the same secret.
website.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL, or post a fixture to the endpoint with the test secret.
website.howWeGoLive: Deploy, set the secret both sides, send one real submission, check it appears in CAR, switch mode to live.
website.howWeDisable: Set the channel mode to off. The endpoint then refuses and says so.
connectSteps: Connect the production website form to the CRM endpoint
Test a new person
Test an existing person
Test filtering and routing

google_form.label: Google Form
google_form.mechanism: Apps Script on the response sheet posts to our endpoint on submit.
google_form.rateLimit: Apps Script quotas apply to the sender, not to us.
google_form.externalBlocker: Somebody who owns the form must paste the script, add the installable trigger and authorise it once.
providerControls: the field names on the form
credentialsNeeded: GOOGLE_FORM_SECRET, generated by us and pasted into the script
google_form.externalActionRequired: The form owner runs the script once and approves the permission prompt.
google_form.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL using the documented Apps Script payload.
google_form.howWeGoLive: Deploy, install the script, submit one real test response, check CAR, switch to live.
google_form.howWeDisable: Remove the trigger at Google, or set the mode to off here.
google_form._note: A second architecture exists - the Forms API with a Cloud project and Pub/Sub. It is heavier and needs a Cloud project. The Apps Script route is what this contract assumes. EXTERNAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED on which one Novikontas wants.
connectSteps: Connect the actual form submission to the CRM
Configure the Apps Script integration
Test a new and an existing person
Test Inbox routing

gmail.label: Email
gmail.mechanism: We poll the Gmail API for new messages. Push over Pub/Sub is possible later.
gmail.rateLimit: Gmail API quota per user. Polling every few minutes is well inside it.
gmail.externalBlocker: Domain-wide delegation for the service account, which only the Google Workspace administrator can grant. Everything on our side is built: the poll route, the JWT assertion with sub=edu@novikontas.org, read-only scope, message flattening and watch expiry.
gmail.externalActionRequired: The Google Workspace administrator authorises domain-wide delegation. This is not something a normal user can do.
gmail.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL with a Gmail-shaped message fixture.
gmail.howWeGoLive: Deploy, add the key, poll once by hand, check CAR, then enable the schedule.
gmail.howWeDisable: Disable the schedule. The key can also be revoked at Google.
gmail.bodyRetention: The message body is held only until somebody qualifies or archives the item, then deleted. What survives is the structured record. Decided 23.09.2026.
connectSteps: **Identify the Google Workspace administrator** - the one thing still unknown
Get authorisation for the Gmail integration
Configure OAuth and the API access
Connect Ieva, Laura and Marina
Test an inbound email into the Inbox

facebook.label: Facebook
facebook.mechanism: Meta sends a webhook to us when a message or lead arrives.
facebook.externalIdSource: the message id, or leadgen_id for a lead form
facebook.timestampSource: the event timestamp, seconds since epoch
facebook.rateLimit: Meta rate limits apply to our calls back to them, not to their webhook.
facebook.externalBlocker: A Meta app, page access from the business portfolio, and APP REVIEW for messaging permissions. Review takes weeks and can be refused.
facebook.externalActionRequired: Confirm WHO owns the page and the business portfolio, create the app, subscribe the page, pass App Review.
facebook.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL with a Meta-shaped webhook body, signed with a test secret.
facebook.howWeGoLive: Deploy, set the callback URL and verify token at Meta, pass the handshake, send one real message, switch to live.
facebook.howWeDisable: Unsubscribe the page at Meta, or set the mode to off here.
facebook.operationalNote: Facebook and Instagram are worked through the shared Meta Business Suite inbox. The channel is Facebook; who owns the person in the CRM is decided after qualification and is not the same question.
connectSteps: Connect the real Facebook Page to the CRM
Configure webhook and API permissions
Test a Facebook message and a lead
Test identity resolution into the Inbox
facebook.handshake: GET the webhook path with hub.mode, hub.verify_token and hub.challenge. We echo the challenge as plain text or Meta will not save the subscription.

mailchimp.mechanism: Audience webhook for subscribe, unsubscribe, profile and cleaned events.
mailchimp.externalIdSource: type + email + fired_at, because Mailchimp sends no event id
mailchimp.rateLimit: Not a concern for inbound events.
credentialsNeeded: a secret we generate and put in the callback URL
mailchimp.externalActionRequired: Somebody with Mailchimp access pastes our address into the Novikontas audience (c6ab4facba) under webhooks. Nothing has to be bought or asked for - checked 24.09.2026.

mailchimp.identityNote: A Mailchimp event is ACTIVITY about somebody, not automatically a new person. It matches on the member id or the email. A newsletter subscriber is not a lead.

Connect the account to the CRM
Map the relevant events
Test through to the Inbox and the Person
mailchimp.handshake: GET the webhook path. Mailchimp checks the URL answers before it will save it, and sends no challenge.

phone._answered: ANSWERED 24.09.2026, and it was in the brief all along. The event carries a `queue` field, and the queue IS the button: 1001*Q-ADMISSION is button 1, 1001*Q-COORDINATORS is button 2, 1001*Q-OTHER is button 3. config/prototype.json -> phoneMenu has mapped it since 23.09.2026. It was listed as an open question by mistake and Ritvars had to point that out.

_meta: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp are reached through ONE Meta Business Suite connection. That is an integration detail. Each remains a SEPARATE channel in the CRM for reporting, filtering, source and history: there is deliberately no combined "Meta" number, because it would hide where people actually came from. WhatsApp being inside the same shared inbox is NOT VERIFIED and must not be claimed.
_blockerKind: question = somebody outside has to answer and the answer may be no. work = the steps are known and nobody has done them yet. A "question" blocker must have an owner in prototype.json -> openQuestions, or nobody chases it. A test enforces that.
_connectOrder: The order Ritvars set on 24.09.2026. Both the Desktop guide and docs/CHANNEL_READINESS.md render in this order, so his list and the generated documents cannot drift apart.
